_help: Lexicon + templates of pipeline/ugc_script.py (the ugc storyboard script engine). Voice is always 'you': no I / my / me / mine (only inside a verbatim review quote). Every line is short, spoken, true for ANY feature that matches its concept; a line that needs a more specific fact carries 'needs' (a regex over the feature's 'TAG line', lower case: the line only fits a feature that says it) and 'not'. An option is a string or {"t": text, "needs": rx, "not": rx}. Words that are claims (anti-theft, hidden pocket, RFID, lockable, water-resistant, scratch-proof, laptop, free shipping ...) never appear in a generic line: compliance.check only lets them through when the product's own facts say them. No number words except 'one' in generic lines (compliance: invented numbers). Spelling: US. concepts: ordered, a feature gets the first concept whose 'match' hits its 'TAG line' (builtin 'tags' first). Fields: rank (arc order: 1 first ... 6 last), travel (fits the travel / crowds angle), adj (superlative hooks: 'the most <adj> bag'), problem (a question that sets up the fix), stop ('Stop ...' imperative), demo (a hands-on opening: 'Watch this.'), headline ('You stop ...' benefit that the concept itself guarantees), after (a third short sentence: a moment or a payoff the concept itself guarantees), moment (scene setter), hook_q / hook_p (a question / problem hook about this concept, <= 14 words), label_p (on-screen label of hook_p), shot_kw (what the picture shows: words of the clip notes in clip_index.json), keywords (caption highlights). words: min / max = the length target of a script of a product with 5+ feature lines (55-80 s at the renderer's pace), aim = what the engine grows a script to (optional chapters first), floor = what lint() accepts, thin_aim = the same aim for a product with fewer feature lines (no minimum: it can only say what it knows).
